experiences.method_family: finite-prefix Li positivity as a global RH certificate
experiences.failure_mode: arbitrarily informative-looking finite sign prefixes can miss off-critical symmetric zero data outside the effective detection range
residual_signature: finite coordinate projection does not control the all-n positivity criterion
off-critical symmetry can remain invisible to hundreds of initial Li transforms
a global proof needs a zeta-specific uniformity mechanism rather than a finite cutoff
broken_assumptions: a sufficiently long verified finite prefix is representative of all Li coefficients
functional-equation and conjugation symmetry alone force early negativity when an off-critical zero exists
scope_conditions: synthetic finite multisets closed under rho->conj(rho) and rho->1-rho
logic that promotes positivity of only finitely many Li transforms without an additional uniform theorem
competing_diagnoses: the failure is merely an artifact of using an arbitrary multiset rather than actual zeta zeros
high imaginary part delays detection while the all-n criterion remains valid
the real missing coordinate is zeta-specific arithmetic structure capable of controlling every n
experiences.selected_diagnosis: finite-prefix positivity loses the infinite-uniformity coordinate; the quartet calibration localizes, but does not solve, the need for a zeta-specific all-n mechanism

residual_signature: positive analytic surrogate does not by itself transport sign to lambda_n
the known all-n norm equality is root-equivalent rather than a cheaper propagation theorem
future progress needs a different representation or a genuinely new unconditional defect decomposition
broken_assumptions: unconditional L2 membership of G_n is enough to infer positivity of lambda_n
model-space innerness and orthonormal-basis structure used in the norm calculation can be imported without RH

experiences.falsifier_or_attempt: execute the preregistered source-dependency matrix and search the unconditional Suzuki 2023 layer for an exact D_n identity, one-sided sign theorem, orthogonality relation, or source term that is strictly weaker than the all-n RH-equivalent norm equality
experiences.observed_result: G_n is unconditionally L2 and Proposition 2.1 is unconditional; the model-space/Hermite-Biehler bridge and Proposition 3.2 are RH-coupled, while Theorem 1.1 makes the all-n norm equality equivalent to RH. No strictly weaker D_n bridge was located inside the registered source boundary.

links.rationale: Both failures preserve the same all-index residual, but their lost coordinates differ: RH-ANA-001 loses the tail by finite projection, whereas RH-ANA-002 retains all indices but loses the target-sign coordinate at the positive-surrogate faithfulness bridge. This is a structural relation, not a causal identification.
